title: Cap. IX Resp.: as to adults — God does not damn without foresight of actual sin; reprobation as denying special grace is from liberty
pass_a_gloss: But let us dismiss infants, and discuss the Major insofar as it regards adults and those having mastery of reason and of free will. As to such, if to deal by strict right be understood as he who decrees someone to be damned and to be affected with eternal death without consideration of actual sin, we confess that God by no means deals by strict right with such sinners. For these he neither damned, nor destined unto damnation, except on account of foresighted sins, and final impenitence in the same. But if by that, to deal by strict right, Corvinus understands not to prepare that special grace, which being applied God knows and establishes that such a man will be freed, or to pass by such a man and not to ordain him unto laying hold of eternal life by the decree of special providence which we call predestination, but to leave him to his (so to speak) deficiency, then we affirm that God so deals with many from the sole liberty of his will: and if this be to deal by strict right (about which we shall soon see), to deal by strict right with all the reprobate.
pass_b_english: Set infants aside and take the Major as it regards adults with reason and free will. If dealing by strict right means decreeing someone damned and afflicted with eternal death without regard to actual sin, we grant God does not so deal with such sinners. He neither damned them nor destined them to damnation except for foresighted sins and final impenitence in them. But if by dealing by strict right Corvinus means not preparing that special grace which, applied, God knows and decrees will free such a man — or passing him by and not ordaining him to take hold of eternal life by the special-providence decree we call predestination, but leaving him to his deficiency (so to speak) — then we affirm God so deals with many from sole liberty of will. And if that is dealing by strict right (we shall see shortly), then he deals by strict right with all the reprobate.
source_text: Sed mittamus infantes, et Majorem discutiamus quatenus adultos et rationis ac liberi arbitrii compotes spectat. Quoad tales, si stricto jure agere intelligatur, qui decernit aliquem damnandum et morte aeterna afficiendum sine consideratione peccati actualis, fatemur Deum cum talibus peccatoribus stricto jure haud agere. Hosce enim neque damnavit, neque damnationi destinavit, nisi ob praevisa peccata, et finalem in iisdem impoenitentiam. Verum si per illud, stricto jure agere, Corvinus intelligat, non praeparare gratiam eam specialem, qua adhibita Deus scit atque statuit talem hominem fore liberandum, vel talem hominem praeterire et ad vitam aeternam capessendam decreto specialis providentiae, quam praedestinationem appellamus, haud ordinare, sed suae (ut ita dicam) deficientiae relinquere, tum affirmamus, Deum cum multis sic agere ex sola libertate voluntatis suae: et si hoc sit stricto jure agere (de quo mox videbimus), stricto jure agere cum omnibus reprobis.
